newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mostly lower after new highs early.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mostly lower after new highs early.

text.p: CME hog futures ended mostly lower after setting new contract highs early as evening up and profit taking developed ahead of Friday's report. Pork bellies also eased to end mixed on profit taking.
October hogs set a new contract high of 57.975 cents per lb and December 57.925 cents before retreating to close 0.225 higher to 0.650 lower with only October up at 57.400 cents.

Profit taking developed after new highs were set as longs, including funds, decided to reduce positions ahead of Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report. However, strong cash markets kept October supported on the break, traders said.

Cash pork product values have advanced the past couple of days, and instances some products posted sharp gains, and this is keeping packer demand for cash hogs strong. Cash hog prices rose $0.50 to $2.00 per cwt Thursday and expectations are for cash markets to trade steady to higher Friday, they said.

Some strength was also attributed to expectations that the report will show lighter than year ago hog numbers and the prospect for increasing hog numbers next year. This added to early gains in nearbys while keeping deferred lean contracts pressured, they added.

Average indications on Friday's quarterly Hogs and Pigs report point to all hogs as of September 1 at 96.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 97.5 percent. Kept for breeding estimates averaged 96.8 percent in a range of 94 to 99 percent and kept for market estimates averaged 96.5 and ranged 95 to 98 percent of last year.

But farrowing intention estimates for September/November and December/February averaged near 100 percent and the high end of expectations ranged from 102 to 105 percent. A figure of 100 percent or more would signal a return to increasing hog production by large producers, they said.
In hog options, First Chicago actively bought December 56 puts and sold 60 calls. Commission houses sold December 58 calls, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures ran up to technical resistance early and then came under profit taking pressure. But support was still evident as cash belly prices rose to highest levels since August 28 at $80 per cwt. Cash bellies have risen despite a farily large hog slaughter rate, traders said.
Pork bellies closed 0.850 cent a lb higher to 0.125 lower with February up 0.750 at 79.250 cents.
